items.title: Floot MCP
items.name: Floot MCP
items.summary: Build and ship web and mobile apps inside Claude or ChatGPT
items.description: Connect Floot to Claude or ChatGPT and build a full-stack app without leaving the chat. Floot gives your AI a ready-to-use workspace with a database, user logins, hosting, and a live URL - nothing to install or configure. Your existing Claude or ChatGPT subscription does the thinking, so Floot doesn’t charge based on AI usage. When you’re ready, publish the same project to the web, iOS, and Android, then keep shipping updates from the same conversation.
top_comments:
Hey Product Hunt - Yuj from Floot here!

Super excited to launch the new Floot MCP - Floot now gives Claude or ChatGPT a zero-setup place to build and publish full-stack apps.

We started Floot a little over a year ago. At the time, we thought a great app builder needed its own AI agent as well as the infrastructure behind it.

That assumption has changed. Claude and ChatGPT have become very good at building software, so creating another agent no longer felt useful. The better product was to give people a simple way to build with the agents they already use.

That’s what Floot MCP does. Connect it once, and Claude or ChatGPT gets a cloud workspace with data, user accounts, hosting, and publishing already set up. There’s nothing to install and no need to wire together separate services. You can keep working on the same project from the web, desktop, or mobile.

Your existing Claude or ChatGPT subscription handles the AI. Floot charges a flat platform fee instead of metering AI usage, which makes it much cheaper than many app builders.

We’ve also just added mobile publishing. The same project can ship to the web, iOS, and Android. Connect your Apple Developer or Google Play account once, then keep shipping from the same conversation where you built the app.

Try out free now on floot.com!

We’d love to see what you make, and I’m happy to answer any questions - thanks so much for the support ❤️
I been using floot since early stage and I can’t stop recommending them, the guys are the best!! And their system keeps improving and improving can’t wait to try this new feature!!

items.title: Hemory
items.name: Hemory
items.summary: Keep listening. Searchable memory for your AI agents.
items.description: Hemory comes from Hear + Memory. It's not meeting transcription: Hemory listens on the phone or Apple Watch you already own, and keeps every conversation as memory. Your day is auto-split into moments with speaker labels, then settles into a private, searchable memory. Connect it to Claude, Codex, Cursor, or any agent over MCP, and your AI finally has real context to revisit what you heard and build on it.
top_comments:
I’m Yingqi, founder of Hemory.

I spend half to two-thirds of my workday in meetings, yet I kept forgetting to start recording—or leaving it running and ending up with several conversations merged into one giant transcript. Even with meeting summaries, piecing together what we’d discussed across different days was still manual work.

So we spent nine months building Hemory: continuous listening that turns everyday conversations into searchable, reusable memory.

Here’s how it works:

- Listen for up to 24 hours: Start with one tap and keep listening in the background with Max.
- Conversations organize themselves: Hemory separates conversations by activity in real time.
- No extra hardware: Use the iPhone, Android phone, or Apple Watch you already own.
- Give your AI real context: Connect Hemory to Codex, OpenClaw, or other compatible AI tools through MCP.

The moment it clicked for me was asking Codex to work with those memories:

“What interesting things did you hear yesterday?”
“Write my half-year review based on what you’ve heard.”
“Pull together our pricing discussions from this month.”

Watching it connect conversations across time and turn them into useful work gave me goosebumps.

Only detected speech counts toward your usage quota.

Our mission: remember what you’ve said and heard—and give your AI the context it needs to help.

Try Hemory at hemory.com, and tell us: what would you ask an AI that remembered your conversations? I’ll be here in the comments all day.

We know you’re happy with CtrlOps as an SSH client.

What if CtrlOps could do more than just connect to your servers?

More listening.

More shipping.

Simplify DevOps.

items.description: Fundraising is broken. Founders spend weeks searching for VCs, researching investment theses, checking sectors, stages and geographies, and sending cold emails, often without knowing who is actually a good fit. Bleetz Network automates the first part of this process. Your AI agent gets matched with 2,000+ SIMULATED agents of real VC, pitches the funds that fit your startup, and gets a YES, NO or MAYBE. A YES unlocks the fund’s contact details. Free, no strings attached.
top_comments: Dear community, I’m the founder of FlowMarket, the world’s first (and, if I’m not mistaken, only) A2A (agent-to-agent) network, where businesses can find suppliers and customers within seconds. In the midst of my fundraising journey, I realised that the whole process is highly broken and inefficient, at least for us founders. There are thousands of VCs worldwide. How do you know which ones are right for you and which aren’t? How do you screen them instantly based on their sector, investment thesis, geography, and other factors? So, I decided to create Bleetz Network (Blitz - the German word for lightning, symbolising speed). We’ve gathered 2,000 VC funds from around the world, enriched them with relevant data, and turned them into simulated VC agents. Your agent gets matched with the right agents, pitches them, and gets one of three answers: YES, NO, or MAYBE, where you get a chance to continue the conversation. If you get a YES, you’ll see the contact details of the fund and its investment team, and the rest is up to you. The platform is completely free, with no strings attached. items.summary: Keep listening. Searchable memory for your AI agents.
items.description: Hemory comes from Hear + Memory. It's not meeting transcription: Hemory listens on the phone or Apple Watch you already own, and keeps every conversation as memory. Your day is auto-split into moments with speaker labels, then settles into a private, searchable memory. Connect it to Claude, Codex, Cursor, or any agent over MCP, and your AI finally has real context to revisit what you heard and build on it.
top_comments:
I’m Yingqi, founder of Hemory.

I spend half to two-thirds of my workday in meetings, yet I kept forgetting to start recording—or leaving it running and ending up with several conversations merged into one giant transcript. Even with meeting summaries, piecing together what we’d discussed across different days was still manual work.

So we spent nine months building Hemory: continuous listening that turns everyday conversations into searchable, reusable memory.

Here’s how it works:

- Listen for up to 24 hours: Start with one tap and keep listening in the background with Max.
- Conversations organize themselves: Hemory separates conversations by activity in real time.
- No extra hardware: Use the iPhone, Android phone, or Apple Watch you already own.
- Give your AI real context: Connect Hemory to Codex, OpenClaw, or other compatible AI tools through MCP.

The moment it clicked for me was asking Codex to work with those memories:

“What interesting things did you hear yesterday?”
“Write my half-year review based on what you’ve heard.”
“Pull together our pricing discussions from this month.”

Watching it connect conversations across time and turn them into useful work gave me goosebumps.

Only detected speech counts toward your usage quota.

Our mission: remember what you’ve said and heard—and give your AI the context it needs to help.

Try Hemory at hemory.com, and tell us: what would you ask an AI that remembered your conversations? I’ll be here in the comments all day.

idea_items.need_line: 法务和律师要把合同审查、文书生成这类重复性法律工作交给 AI，但通用模型给出的结论颗粒度太粗，不敢直接采用。

interest_sections.title: 法律 AI 工作流
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 zhihu、GitHub，核心观察是法律 AI 的争论点已经从“能不能替代人审合同”下沉到审到什么颗粒度、依据能否被律师复核，而条文与判决公开这一数据条件正被当成可自建工作流的前提。

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 现状是通用模型加现成工具混用——有人直接拿 ChatGPT 类模型处理合同，有人上 Ironclad、律己 AI、幂律智能这类已有商业产品做审查和全生命周期管理，GitHub 上也出现用 LangChain Agent 接法律数据库 API 自建咨询、审查、文书生成的项目，讨论仍集中在“AI 能不能审得准”而非具体条款颗粒度。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的是把公开法律条文与裁判文书做成可检索底座，让模型对具体条款输出带引用出处、可逐条核对的判断结果，而不是只给一段笼统的修改建议。

interest_sections.title: AI 应用场景 / 数据
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 zhihu，核心观察是场景梳理的卡点不在方法论而在“把业务讲清楚”的成图产出一环，当前仍靠人工画图和模板复述撑着。

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 现状是靠 Xmind 一类思维导图工具手动画图，讨论集中在三类图各自用在哪、结构图该问哪几个问题、以及通用流程模板怎么套。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的是能把一段业务描述或需求文本直接拆成结构/流程/架构三类图、并保留模块层级以便查漏补缺的自动成图能力。

interest_sections.title: 语言 AI 陪练
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 zhihu，口语能力长期被阅读教学压制，用户正转向能对自选内容进行精细化纠错的工具型陪练。

items.title: 需求
items.paragraph: 口语学习者最直接的需求是开口练习时能知道自己哪个音节读错，而不是只得到一个笼统的好坏评价

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 目前讨论集中在开源工具 Enjoy 的跟读与纠音方案上，它能对用户上传的视频自动生成字幕分段，并指出具体发音错误音节。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的方向是利用用户自选的真实语料（美剧、视频）生成带逐句评分与音节级反馈的口语练习，而非另造一套固定对话教材。

interest_sections.title: 简历优化助手
interest_sections.summary: 这一组信号主要来自 zhihu，核心观察是简历焦虑已从排版美化转向如何在不造假、不合并经历的前提下，化解跳槽频繁与经历断档带来的初筛淘汰和面试追问风险。

items.title: 需求
items.paragraph: 求职者最明确的需求是把"五年五跳"或学历偏低这类硬伤经历，重组成能扛住HR三五秒初筛、又在面试深挖时不说漏的稳定叙事

items.title: 现状
items.paragraph: 现状是求职者要么合并前几段经历、把专科写成本科先骗到面邀再坦白，要么把前项目的业务逻辑图和流程图背熟以应对简历深挖，HR侧则对三年三跳、五年五跳的简历基本扫几眼就叉掉。

items.title: 方向跟踪
items.paragraph: 值得跟踪的是把目标岗位JD与HR淘汰习惯前置，做成"稳定性叙事重排＋面试深挖问答预演"的简历诊断方向，而非停留在措辞润色。
